paper_title: The Complexity of Reachability Problems in Strongly Connected Finite Automata
classifications: Theory of computation → Formal languages and automata theory
statement: The class of k-image-bounded NFAs seems to be worth further investigation. The property is natural, but we did not find it mentioned in the literature. It is easy to see that an incomplete k-image-bounded NFA always admits a mortal word of length at most nk+1 . Is this bound tight?
context: Another interesting open problem of the same spirit is finding subclasses of NFAs where the considered problems are not NL-hard. Such subclasses are likely to have new interesting properties and characterisation. In particular, one can ask for subclasses where a random word of polynomial length provides a yes-certificate with high probability. This would immediately imply that the corresponding reachability problem is in the randomised counterpart of L for such a subclass. The class of k-image-bounded NFAs seems to be worth further investigation. The property is natural, but we did not find it mentioned in the literature. It is easy to see that an incomplete k-image-bounded NFA always admits a mortal word of length at most nk+1 . Is this bound tight?
